**TL;DR** Generalizes causal abstraction to mechanism transformations and shows how it formalizes graded faithfulness and unifies mechanistic interpretability methods.
**Problem** Interpretable algorithms need a precise connection to opaque model mechanisms; neuron-level interventions cannot isolate overlapping distributed features.
**Method** Intervention algebras; exact and approximate transformations; bijective translations; constructive abstractions; interchange interventions.
**Findings** Formalizes modular features and graded faithfulness; decomposes constructive abstraction into three operations; expresses many interpretability methods within one framework.
**Limits** Deterministic setting; faithfulness depends on intervention coverage, similarity and aggregation choices; does not establish that an abstraction is uniquely explanatory.

**Relations**
- builds-on [[jacovi2020towards]]: formalizes its requirement that faithfulness be graded and sensitive to the evaluation setting

definitions.quote: A (deterministic) causal model is a pair M = (Σ, {FX }X∈V ), such that Σ is a signature and {FX }X∈V is a set of mechanisms, with FX : ValV → ValX assigning a value to X as a function of the values of all the variables, including X itself.
definitions.formula: M=(\Sigma,\{F_X\}_{X\in\mathbf V}),\qquad F_X:\operatorname{Val}_{\mathbf V}\to\operatorname{Val}_X.
definitions.assumptions: A signature specifying variables and their nonempty value ranges; deterministic mechanisms.
definitions.gloss: A collection of variables and equations specifying their causal mechanisms.
definitions.relation: Underlying model class for exact transformation and constructive abstraction; permits cycles and self-dependence.

definitions.quote: The resulting order ≺ captures a notion of direct causation, which can be extended to indirect causation by taking its transitive closure ≺∗ .
definitions.formula: Y\prec X\iff\exists\mathbf z,y,y'\;F_X(\mathbf z,y)\ne F_X(\mathbf z,y'),\qquad\mathbf Z=\mathbf V\setminus\{Y\};\qquad\prec^*=\operatorname{TC}(\prec).
definitions.assumptions: Known deterministic mechanisms; other variables held fixed while varying Y.
definitions.gloss: Direct causation is functional dependence; indirect causation follows chains of such dependence.
definitions.relation: Defines the graphical structure induced by the causal model; distinct from an actual-causation definition.

definitions.quote: Given M = (V, {FX }X∈V ), the set of solutions, called Solve(M), is the set of all v ∈ ValV such that all the equations ProjX (v) = FX (v) are satisfied for each X ∈ V.
definitions.formula: \operatorname{Solve}(M)=\{\mathbf v\in\operatorname{Val}_{\mathbf V}:\forall X\in\mathbf V,\ \operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathbf v)=F_X(\mathbf v)\}.
definitions.assumptions: Known mechanisms; cyclic models may have no solution or multiple solutions.
definitions.gloss: All complete states that satisfy the model's equations simultaneously.
definitions.relation: Exact transformations preserve these sets after corresponding interventions.

definitions.quote: Define a hard intervention to be a partial setting i ∈ ValI for finite I ⊆ V.
definitions.formula: F_X^{\mathbf i}(\mathbf v)=\begin{cases}\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathbf i),&X\in\mathbf I,\\F_X(\mathbf v),&X\notin\mathbf I.\end{cases}
definitions.assumptions: A causal model and a finite set of variables to fix.
definitions.gloss: Replace selected mechanisms with constants.
definitions.relation: Special case of soft intervention and interventional.

definitions.quote: We define a soft intervention on some finite set of variables X ⊆ V to be a family of functions {IX }X∈X where IX : ValV → ValX for each X ∈ X.
definitions.formula: I=\{I_X\}_{X\in\mathbf X},\quad I_X:\operatorname{Val}_{\mathbf V}\to\operatorname{Val}_X;\qquad F_X^I=I_X\ \text{for }X\in\mathbf X.
definitions.assumptions: Replacement mechanisms on a finite set of variables.
definitions.gloss: Replace selected mechanisms with new functions.
definitions.relation: Generalizes hard intervention; special case of interventional.

definitions.quote: We define an interventional on some finite set of variables X ⊆ V to be a family of functions I = {IX }X∈X where IX : SoftX → SoftX for each X ∈ X.
definitions.formula: I=\{I_X\}_{X\in\mathbf X},\qquad I_X:\operatorname{Soft}_X\to\operatorname{Soft}_X,\qquad F_X^I=I_X\langle F_X\rangle.
definitions.assumptions: Access to mechanisms; transformations may depend on the mechanisms being replaced.
definitions.gloss: Transform mechanisms using functions of the original mechanisms.
definitions.relation: Generalizes soft interventions beyond mechanism replacement.

definitions.quote: An intervention algebra formalizes the notion of a set of separable components with distinct mechanisms, satisfying the fundamental algebraic properties of commutativity and left-annihilativity (see (a) and (b) in Definition 16).
definitions.formula: (\Lambda,\oplus)\text{ is an intervention algebra}\iff\exists\Sigma\;(\Lambda,\oplus)\simeq(\Phi_\Sigma,\circ),
definitions.assumptions: A binary operation; ΦΣ is the algebra of finite hard interventions for some signature.
definitions.gloss: An intervention system with the same algebraic structure as hard interventions.
definitions.relation: Restricts general interventionals so they behave like interventions on separable variables.

definitions.quote: These two properties highlight an important sense in which hard interventions are modular: when intervening on two different variables, the order does not matter; and when intervening on the same variable twice, the second undoes any effect of the first intervention.
definitions.formula: X\ne Y\Rightarrow x\circ y=y\circ x;\qquad X=Y\Rightarrow x\circ y=y.
definitions.assumptions: Atomic interventions; composition follows the paper's left-to-right intervention convention.
definitions.gloss: Different components can be edited independently; a later edit of one component replaces its earlier edit.
definitions.relation: Characterizes the modular behavior captured by intervention algebras.

definitions.quote: Then M∗ is an exact transformation of M under (τ, ω) if for all I ∈ Domain(ω), the following diagram commutes:
definitions.formula: \forall I\in\operatorname{Domain}(\omega),\qquad\tau\bigl(\operatorname{Solve}(M_I)\bigr)=\operatorname{Solve}\bigl(M^*_{\omega(I)}\bigr).
definitions.assumptions: Intervention algebras on both models; partial surjections τ and ω; ω preserves the intervention order. Undefined τ values receive a distinguished bottom value.
definitions.gloss: Intervening and then translating yields exactly the same states as translating the intervention and running the other model.
definitions.relation: Generalizes deterministic uniform transformation to interventionals; includes bijective translation and constructive abstraction.

definitions.quote: We say that τ (M) is the bijective translation of M under τ .
definitions.formula: F_{X^*}^{\tau(M)}(\mathbf v^*)=\operatorname{Proj}_{X^*}\!\left(\tau\left(F_{\mathbf V}(\tau^{-1}(\mathbf v^*))\right)\right).
definitions.assumptions: A bijection between complete state spaces; known mechanisms.
definitions.gloss: Rewrite the same mechanisms in an invertibly transformed state space.
definitions.relation: Lossless special case of exact transformation; supplies access to distributed modular features.

definitions.quote: In words, the set ΠXH consists of those low-level variables that are ‘aligned’ with the high-level variable XH , and πXH tells us how a given setting of the low-level cluster ΠXH corresponds to a setting of the high-level variable XH .
definitions.formula: \Pi=\{\Pi_X:X\in\mathbf V_H\}\cup\{\Pi_\bot\}\text{ partitions }\mathbf V_L;\quad\Pi_X\ne\varnothing;\quad\pi_X:\operatorname{Val}_{\Pi_X}\rightharpoonup\operatorname{Val}_X\text{ is surjective}.\qquad\tau^\pi(\mathbf v)=\bigcup_{X\in\mathbf V_H}\pi_X(\operatorname{Proj}_{\Pi_X}(\mathbf v)).
definitions.assumptions: Nonoverlapping variable clusters; a possibly empty forgotten cluster; partial surjective value maps.
definitions.gloss: Specify which low-level variables realize each high-level variable and how their values correspond.
definitions.relation: Canonically induces the state map τπ and intervention map ωπ used in constructive abstraction.

definitions.quote: We say that H is a constructive abstraction of L under an alignment ⟨Π, π⟩ iff H is an exact transformation of L under (τ π , ω π ).
definitions.formula: \forall\mathbf i\in\operatorname{Domain}(\omega^\pi),\qquad\tau^\pi(\operatorname{Solve}(L_{\mathbf i}))=\operatorname{Solve}(H_{\omega^\pi(\mathbf i)}).
definitions.assumptions: An alignment; ωπ acts on interventions targeting complete aligned cells, excluding the forgotten cell.
definitions.gloss: The high-level model preserves interventions under a specified clustering of low-level variables.
definitions.relation: Special case of exact transformation; permits partial value maps unlike Beckers and Halpern's original constructive abstraction.

definitions.quote: Marginalization is essentially a matter of ignoring a subset X of variables.
definitions.formula: \mathbf V^*=\mathbf V\setminus\mathbf X,\qquad\Pi_\bot=\mathbf X,\qquad\Pi_Y=\{Y\},\quad\pi_Y(y)=y\quad(Y\notin\mathbf X).
definitions.assumptions: A signature and a proper subset of variables to forget.
definitions.gloss: Forget selected variables while retaining the values of the others.
definitions.relation: One of three operations sufficient to decompose any alignment.

definitions.quote: Next, variable merge collapses each cell of a partition into single variables.
definitions.formula: \operatorname{Val}_{X^*}^*=\operatorname{Val}_{\Pi_{X^*}},\qquad\Pi_\bot=\varnothing,\qquad\pi_{X^*}(\mathbf y)=\mathbf y.
definitions.assumptions: A partition of low-level variables indexed by the new high-level variables.
definitions.gloss: Replace each variable cluster with one variable retaining the cluster's complete joint value.
definitions.relation: One of the three alignment-decomposition operations; does not itself discard values.

definitions.quote: Finally, value merge alters the value space of each variable, potentially collapsing values:
definitions.formula: \delta_X:\operatorname{Val}_X\rightharpoonup\operatorname{Val}_X^*\text{ surjective},\qquad\Pi_X=\{X\},\quad\Pi_\bot=\varnothing,\quad\pi_X=\delta_X.
definitions.assumptions: A partial surjective map to a new value space for each variable.
definitions.gloss: Coarsen variable values while retaining the variables.
definitions.relation: Complements marginalization and variable merge in decomposing constructive alignments.

definitions.quote: Composition of alignments is defined, as expected, via composition of their maps.
definitions.formula: \Pi''_{X''}=\bigcup_{X'\in\Pi'_{X''}}\Pi_{X'},\qquad\Pi''_\bot=\bigcup_{X'\in\Pi'_\bot\cup\{\bot\}}\Pi_{X'},\qquad\pi''_{X''}(\mathbf y)=\pi'_{X''}\!\left(\bigcup_{X'\in\Pi'_{X''}}\pi_{X'}(\operatorname{Proj}_{\Pi_{X'}}(\mathbf y))\right).
definitions.assumptions: Two alignments with matching intermediate signatures.
definitions.gloss: Combine two successive abstraction alignments into one.
definitions.relation: Used in the decomposition of alignments into marginalization, variable merge and value merge.

definitions.quote: Taken together, we can construct a metric that quantifies the degree to which M∗ is an approximate transformation of M in a single number:
definitions.formula: \mathcal S_{I\sim P}\!\left[\operatorname{Sim}\!\left(\tau(\operatorname{Solve}(M_I)),\operatorname{Solve}(M^*_{\omega(I)})\right)\right].
definitions.assumptions: Partial surjective state and order-preserving intervention maps; a similarity function, intervention distribution P and real-valued aggregation statistic S; evaluable solved states.
definitions.where: §2.4, Definition 41, Eq. 6, [P224]–[P226]; interpretation as graded faithfulness in §3.2, [P592]
definitions.gloss: Grade an interpretation by aggregating agreement under corresponding interventions.
definitions.relation: Graded version of exact transformation; encompasses interchange intervention accuracy, LIME fidelity and other choices of comparison metric.

concepts: faithfulness of reasoning, explanations or self-reports
definitions.quote: If this number is above a particular cutoff η, we can say that M∗ is an η-approximate abstraction of M.
definitions.formula: \mathcal S_{I\sim P}[\operatorname{Sim}(\tau(\operatorname{Solve}(M_I)),\operatorname{Solve}(M^*_{\omega(I)}))]>\eta.
definitions.assumptions: The approximate-transformation score and a threshold; the quoted direction assumes larger scores indicate better agreement.
definitions.gloss: Accept an abstraction when its graded score exceeds a specified threshold.
definitions.relation: Thresholded approximate transformation; the paper states an above-threshold convention despite also allowing distance-valued comparisons.

definitions.quote: Specifically, the causal model is provided a ‘base’ input and an intervention is performed that fixes some variables to be the values they would have if different ‘source’ inputs were provided.
definitions.formula: \operatorname{IntInv}(M,\langle\mathbf s_1,\ldots,\mathbf s_k\rangle,\langle\mathbf X_1,\ldots,\mathbf X_k\rangle)=\bigcup_{j=1}^k\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_j}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf s_j})).
definitions.assumptions: Input variables; disjoint noninput target sets; source computations supplying definite target values.
definitions.gloss: Patch selected variables with values produced by other inputs.
definitions.relation: Base case for recursive interchange interventions and distributed interchange interventions.

definitions.quote: We take interchange interventions as a base case and generalize to recursive interchange interventions, where variables are fixed to be the value they would have if a recursive interchange intervention (that itself may be defined in terms of other interchange interventions) were performed.
definitions.formula: \operatorname{RecIntInv}_{m+1}(M,\langle\mathbf s_j\rangle,\langle\mathbf X_j\rangle,\langle\mathbf i_j\rangle)=\bigcup_{j=1}^k\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_j}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf s_j\circ\mathbf i_j}));\qquad\operatorname{RecIntInv}_0=\operatorname{IntInv}.
definitions.assumptions: Disjoint target sets and depth-m interventions used in the source computations.
definitions.gloss: Patch with values obtained from computations that themselves contain patches.
definitions.relation: Generalizes interchange intervention; expresses path patching and causal scrubbing operations.

definitions.quote: Geiger et al. (2023) generalize interchange interventions to distributed interchange interventions that target variables distributed across multiple causal variables.
definitions.formula: F_X\leftarrow\left[\mathbf v\mapsto\operatorname{Proj}_X\!\left(\tau^{-1}\!\left(\operatorname{Solve}\!\left(\tau(M)_{\operatorname{IntInv}(M,\langle\mathbf s_1,\ldots,\mathbf s_k\rangle,\langle\mathbf X_1^*,\ldots,\mathbf X_k^*\rangle)}\right)\right)\right)\right].
definitions.assumptions: An input-preserving bijective translation and disjoint targets in the translated space. Formula follows the printed Definition 46, including its use of M inside IntInv.
definitions.gloss: Translate to a feature space, patch there, and translate back.
definitions.relation: Extends interchange interventions to distributed features using bijective translation.

concepts: faithfulness of reasoning, explanations or self-reports
definitions.quote: Geiger et al. (2022b) propose interchange intervention accuracy, which is simply the proportion of interchange interventions where the low-level and high-level causal models have the same input–output behavior (see Section 2.6 for an example).
definitions.formula: \operatorname{IIA}(H,L,(\Pi,\pi))=\mathbb E_{\mathbf i\sim P(\operatorname{Domain}(\omega^\pi))}\!\left[\mathbf1\!\left[\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_H^{\mathrm{Out}}}(\tau^\pi(L_{\mathbf i}))=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_H^{\mathrm{Out}}}(H_{\omega^\pi(\mathbf i)})\right]\right].
definitions.assumptions: An aligned model pair and a distribution over aligned interventions; intervened-model notation denotes its resulting state.
definitions.gloss: How often corresponding patches make the two models produce matching outputs.
definitions.relation: Special case of approximate transformation with output equality and expectation; ordinary accuracy results when base and source inputs coincide.

definitions.quote: We propose to define modular features as any set of variables that form an intervention algebra accessed by a bijective translation.
definitions.formula: \text{Modular features are variables of }\tau(M)\text{ accessed through bijective }\tau\text{ whose interventions form an intervention algebra}.
definitions.assumptions: A bijective translation and an intervention algebra; no linearity restriction.
definitions.gloss: Separable causal components exposed by an invertible change of representation.
definitions.relation: Uses bijective translation and intervention algebra to generalize neuron-aligned and linear features.

concepts: faithfulness of reasoning, explanations or self-reports
definitions.quote: The LIME fidelity of using H to interpret L on the input x is given as:
definitions.formula: \operatorname{LIME}(H,L,\Delta_{\mathbf x})=\frac1{|\Delta_{\mathbf x}|}\sum_{\mathbf x'\in\Delta_{\mathbf x}}\operatorname{Distance}\!\left(\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_L^{\mathrm{Out}}}(\operatorname{Solve}(L_{\mathbf x'})),\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_H^{\mathrm{Out}}}(\operatorname{Solve}(H_{\mathbf x'}))\right).
definitions.assumptions: Identical input/output spaces; a finite neighborhood of inputs and an output-distance function.
definitions.gloss: Average local output disagreement between an interpretable model and the model it explains.
definitions.relation: Special case of approximate transformation restricted to input interventions; does not establish agreement of internal mechanisms.

definitions.quote: Given a neural network as a causal model M, we define the integrated gradient value of the ith neuron of an hidden vector Y when the network is provided x as an input as follows, where y′ is the so-called baseline value of Y:
definitions.formula: \operatorname{IG}_i(\mathbf y,\mathbf y')=(y_i-y_i')\int_0^1\frac{\partial\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X^{\mathrm{Out}}}(M_{\mathbf x\cup(\delta\mathbf y+(1-\delta)\mathbf y')})}{\partial y_i}\,d\delta.
definitions.assumptions: A differentiable network, a hidden vector, an input and a baseline; numerical outputs.
definitions.gloss: Attribute an output difference by integrating gradients between baseline and actual hidden states.
definitions.relation: Its completeness axiom allows reconstruction of single-source interchange-intervention effects.

definitions.term: completeness axiom of the integrated gradients method
concepts: faithfulness of reasoning, explanations or self-reports
definitions.quote: The completeness axiom of the integrated gradients method is formulated as follows:
definitions.formula: \sum_{i=1}^{|\mathbf Y|}\operatorname{IG}_i(\mathbf y,\mathbf y')=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X^{\mathrm{Out}}}(M_{\mathbf x\cup\mathbf y})-\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X^{\mathrm{Out}}}(M_{\mathbf x\cup\mathbf y'}).
definitions.assumptions: The integrated-gradients setup and conditions under which the path integral is defined.
definitions.gloss: Attributions sum to the output change caused by replacing the baseline hidden state.
definitions.relation: Completeness of numerical attribution, rather than completeness of a natural-language reasoning explanation.

definitions.quote: The fundamental notions involved in mediation are total, direct, and indirect effects, which can be defined with interchange interventions.
definitions.formula: \begin{aligned}\operatorname{TotalEffect}(M,\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathbf Y)&=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf Y}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf x'}))-\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf Y}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf x})),\\\operatorname{DirectEffect}(M,\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathbf Y,\mathbf Z)&=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf Y}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf x'\cup\operatorname{IntInv}(M,\langle\mathbf x\rangle,\langle\mathbf Z\rangle)}))-\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf Y}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf x})),\\\operatorname{IndirectEffect}(M,\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathbf Y,\mathbf Z)&=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf Y}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf x\cup\operatorname{IntInv}(M,\langle\mathbf x'\rangle,\langle\mathbf Z\rangle)}))-\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf Y}(\operatorname{Solve}(M_{\mathbf x})).\end{aligned}
definitions.assumptions: Disjoint X, Y and Z; subtraction of Y values is defined; source and intervened computations have definite solutions.
definitions.gloss: Compare the full input change with changes that freeze or selectively change the mediator.
definitions.relation: Defines mediation effects using interchange interventions; complete mediation equates indirect and total effects.

definitions.quote: The following are equivalent:
definitions.formula: \operatorname{IndirectEffect}(L,\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathbf X^{\mathrm{Out}},\mathbf H)=\operatorname{TotalEffect}(M,\mathbf x,\mathbf x',\mathbf X^{\mathrm{Out}}),\qquad M=L.
definitions.assumptions: A neural network, specified inputs/outputs and candidate hidden mediator; the displayed equation switches from L to M for the same network.
definitions.gloss: Changing the mediator alone reproduces the entire effect of changing the input.
definitions.relation: A criterion expressed through total and indirect effects; related to abstraction by an input–mediator–output chain.

definitions.quote: To perform a path patch, we use a recursive interchange intervention on a model M processing a base input b that simulates ‘sender’ variables H taking on intervened values from a source input s, restricting the effect of this intervention to receiver variables R while freezing variables F.
definitions.formula: \mathbf i_R=\operatorname{IntInv}(M,\langle\mathbf s,\mathbf b\rangle,\langle\mathbf H,\mathbf F\setminus\{R\}\rangle);\qquad\mathbf j=\operatorname{RecIntInv}(M,\langle\mathbf b,\ldots,\mathbf b\rangle,\langle R_1,\ldots,R_2\rangle,\langle\mathbf i_{R_1},\ldots,\mathbf i_{R_k}\rangle).
definitions.assumptions: Base/source inputs, sender/receiver sets and frozen variables. The printed receiver list ends in R2 although the text indexes k receivers.
definitions.gloss: Patch a sender's influence into selected receivers while freezing alternative routes.
definitions.relation: An application of recursive interchange interventions.

definitions.quote: If performing an ablation on H to erase the concept C leads L to have the degraded behavior AC without changing other behaviors, then the ablation was successful.
definitions.formula: \operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_L^{\mathrm{Out}}}(\operatorname{Solve}((L_I)_{\mathbf x}))=\begin{cases}A_C(\mathbf x),&\mathbf x\in\operatorname{Domain}(A_C),\\\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_L^{\mathrm{Out}}}(\operatorname{Solve}(L_{\mathbf x})),&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}
definitions.assumptions: A proposed concept-erasing ablation and a specified partial function describing the behavioral degradation expected from erasing that concept.
definitions.gloss: Erasure causes the concept-specific deficit while preserving other behavior.
definitions.relation: Equivalent to exact transformation by the section's three-variable ablation model.

definitions.quote: The high-level causal model H is an exact transformation of the low-level neural model L under (τ, ω) exactly when the subcircuit C preserves the behavior B.
definitions.formula: \forall\mathbf x\in\operatorname{Domain}(B),\qquad\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbf X_L^{\mathrm{Out}}}(\operatorname{Solve}((L_{I_{\overline C}})_{\mathbf x}))=B(\mathbf x),\qquad\overline C=\mathbf V\times\mathbf V\setminus C.
definitions.assumptions: A candidate circuit, a target behavior and specified ablation values for connections outside the circuit.
definitions.gloss: The candidate circuit still realizes the target behavior after its complement is ablated.
definitions.relation: Expressed as exact transformation by a three-variable ablation model; causal scrubbing uses a different intervention scheme.

concepts: faithfulness of reasoning, explanations or self-reports
definitions.quote: Chan et al. (2022b) propose to measure the faithfulness of H by appeal to the proportion of performance maintained by L under interventionals determined by Scrub.
definitions.formula: \mathbb E_{I\sim P}\!\left[\mathbf1\!\left[\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathrm{Out}}(\tau(\operatorname{Solve}(L_I)))=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathrm{Out}}(\operatorname{Solve}(H^*_{\omega(I)}))\right]\right].
definitions.assumptions: The Scrub algorithm, its source-sampling distributions, the target behavior and the auxiliary ablation model H* constructed in §3.5.2.
definitions.gloss: Measure behavior preserved after recursively resampling connections according to a proposed interpretation.
definitions.relation: Special case of approximate transformation with indicator similarity and expectation; H* differs from the interpretation H used to choose resamples.

**TL;DR** Defines approximate causal abstraction by measuring discrepancies between intervention outcomes, extending exact abstraction to deterministic and probabilistic models.
**Problem** Exact causal abstraction excludes useful scientific models whose coarse predictions are only approximately correct.
**Method** Lift state-space distances to model distances; optimize context mappings; add probabilistic contexts and intervention distributions.
**Findings** Zero-error cases recover exact abstraction; establishes composition results and constructive decomposition guarantees.
**Limits** Finite signatures; application-dependent distances and intervention choices; general approximate abstractions need not decompose into approximation and exact abstraction.

**Relations**
- (none)

definitions.quote: Intuitively, [Y1 ← y1 , . . . , Yk ← yk ]ϕ says that ϕ would hold if Yi were set to yi , for i = 1, . . . , k.
definitions.formula: (M,\mathbf u)\models[\mathbf Y\leftarrow\mathbf y]\varphi\iff(M_{\mathbf Y\leftarrow\mathbf y},\mathbf u)\models\varphi.
definitions.assumptions: A recursive causal model; a fixed exogenous context; φ is a Boolean combination of endogenous-variable assignments.
definitions.gloss: Evaluate a claim after replacing selected structural equations with fixed values.
definitions.relation: Counterfactual semantics underlying the intervention-outcome distances.

definitions.quote: We briefly review the relevant definitions here; we refer the reader to their paper for more details and motivation.
definitions.formula: \operatorname{Rst}(\mathbf V,\mathbf x)=\{\mathbf v\in\mathcal R(\mathbf V):\mathbf v|_{\mathbf X}=\mathbf x\};\qquad\omega_\tau(\mathbf X\leftarrow\mathbf x)=\mathbf Y\leftarrow\mathbf y\iff\tau(\operatorname{Rst}(\mathbf V_L,\mathbf x))=\operatorname{Rst}(\mathbf V_H,\mathbf y).\qquad\mathcal I_L^\tau=\operatorname{Domain}(\omega_\tau),\quad\mathcal I_H^\tau=\omega_\tau(\mathcal I_L^\tau).
definitions.assumptions: A low-to-high state map; ωτ is undefined when the image is not a high-level restriction set.
definitions.gloss: Derive intervention correspondence directly from which states each intervention fixes.
definitions.relation: Reproduces Beckers and Halpern's induced intervention map; used in τ-consistency and τ-abstraction.

definitions.quote: We capture all of them by requiring the two causal models to be τ -consistent:
definitions.formula: \tau:\mathcal R_L(\mathbf V_L)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal R_H(\mathbf V_H),\qquad\mathcal I_H=\omega_\tau(\mathcal I_L),\qquad|\mathcal R_L(\mathbf U_L)|\ge|\mathcal R_H(\mathbf U_H)|.
definitions.assumptions: Two causal-model signatures, allowed intervention sets and a state map.
definitions.gloss: Require compatible state spaces, intervention sets and enough low-level contexts to cover high-level contexts.
definitions.relation: Necessary structural prerequisites for exact and approximate τ-abstraction.

definitions.quote: Abstraction means that for each possible low-level context-intervention pair, the two ways of moving up “diagonally” to a high-level endogenous state always lead to the same result.
definitions.formula: \exists\tau_U:\mathcal R_L(\mathbf U_L)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal R_H(\mathbf U_H)\;\forall\mathbf u_L,i\in\mathcal I_L,\quad\tau(M_L(\mathbf u_L,i))=M_H(\tau_U(\mathbf u_L),\omega_\tau(i)),
definitions.assumptions: τ-consistent models; the context quantifier ranges over all low-level contexts, independently of the intervention quantifier.
definitions.gloss: Every allowed intervention has exactly corresponding outcomes at both levels in every context.
definitions.relation: Inherited from Abstracting Causal Models; recovered by zero-error deterministic approximate abstraction.

definitions.quote: If MH is a τ -abstraction of ML then we say it is constructive if τ is constructive and IL = ILτ .
definitions.formula: \mathbf V_L=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{n+1}\mathbf Z_i,\quad\mathbf Z_i\ne\varnothing\ (i\le n),\quad\tau(\mathbf v_L)=\tau_1(\mathbf v_L|_{\mathbf Z_1})\cdots\tau_n(\mathbf v_L|_{\mathbf Z_n}),\quad\tau_i:\mathcal R(\mathbf Z_i)\to\mathcal R(Y_i).\qquad\text{Constructive abstraction additionally requires }\mathcal I_L=\mathcal I_L^\tau.
definitions.assumptions: High-level variables Y1,…,Yn; a partition with a possibly empty forgotten cell.
definitions.gloss: Each high-level variable is computed from its own disjoint low-level variable cluster.
definitions.relation: Supplies the constructive special case used in the decomposition theorem.

definitions.quote: We start with the simplest setting where this intuition can be made precise, one where the models M1 and M2 differ only with regards to their equations. We say that two models are similar in this case.
definitions.formula: M_1=(\mathcal S,\mathcal F_1,\mathcal I),\qquad M_2=(\mathcal S,\mathcal F_2,\mathcal I).
definitions.assumptions: The same signature, allowed interventions and state metric; probabilistic similarity also retains the context distribution.
definitions.gloss: Models are similar when only their structural equations differ.
definitions.relation: Allows direct approximation without a change of representational level.

definitions.quote: Thus, M1 is a dmax -α approximation of M2 if the predictions of M1 are always within α of the predictions of M2 .
definitions.formula: d_{\max}(M_1,M_2)=\max_{i\in\mathcal I,\ \mathbf u\in\mathcal R(\mathbf U)}d_{\mathbf V}(M_1(\mathbf u,i),M_2(\mathbf u,i));\qquad d_{\max}(M_1,M_2)\le\alpha.

definitions.quote: The following definitions about τ -abstractions from Beckers & Halpern (2019) set the groundwork for many discussions on abstraction theory.

definitions.assumptions: A strong abstraction and a disjoint low-level variable partition.

definitions.formula: C_i\to C_j\in E_{\mathcal C}\iff\exists V_i\in C_i,V_j\in C_j:\ V_i\to V_j\in E;\qquad C_i\leftrightarrow C_j\in E_{\mathcal C}\iff\exists V_i\in C_i,V_j\in C_j:\ V_i\leftrightarrow V_j\in E.

**TL;DR** Shows that unrestricted alignment maps can make causal abstraction vacuous, and complex maps yield high intervention accuracy even for random models.
**Problem** Causal abstraction permits alignment maps powerful enough to supply the apparent algorithm themselves.
**Method** Existence proof; identity, orthogonal and reversible nonlinear alignments; equality, Boolean-law and indirect-object tasks.
**Findings** Under stated assumptions, arbitrary algorithms align; random language models reach perfect intervention accuracy; disjoint-name generalization fails for random models.
**Limits** Theorem requires countability, injectivity, strict output-surjectivity, compatible computational order and correct task behavior; existence does not establish learnability.

definitions.quote: The non-linear representation hypothesis (Pimentel et al., 2020b) argues that information may be encoded in arbitrary non-linear subspaces of a neural network.
definitions.assumptions: Allows nonlinear encodings without restricting alignment-map complexity.
definitions.gloss: Relevant information may require nonlinear transformations to access.
